al_buzzards_roost.blurb: A compact limestone bouldering spot on the Monte Sano side of Huntsville, built around a single roof with a few other lines nearby. Seven problems in all, none of them easy: the range starts around V3, sits mostly in the V5 to V8 band, and the hardest few top out near V8. The movement is on the steep roof with good holds, and the landing has been tidied to make falling less punishing. It is close to town, a short and gentle hike from the city, which makes it a handy evening session for strong boulderers rather than a place for beginners.

al_the_chonk.blurb: A freestanding sandstone tower in the gorge at Noccalula Falls near Gadsden, sitting just north of the creek bed. Six sport lines and one boulder problem share the formation, and the sport routes are all hard: the easiest sits around 5.10 and most are 5.11 to 5.12. The tower has an odd lean that produces unusual moves, and a hanging arete on it is considered a standout for the whole canyon. The boulder problem on the south side is a high-end V8. Lowering anchors are in place on every line. Expect a short scramble and a drainage trail to reach the base.

al_hope_boulder.blurb: The first boulder you meet on the Middle Bishop trail at Bishop Mountain, close to the car and used as a warm-up before heading uphill to the main cluster. Seven limestone problems, all on the easy end: they run from V0 up to V3, with most at V1 and V2. That makes it a friendly place to loosen up or to bring newer boulderers. Bishop Mountain lies outside Huntsville, reached along the highway toward Guntersville.
al_hope_boulder.approach: A one-to-two minute walk straight into the woods from the parking area; the boulder is the first one you pass.

_expect.name: I'm not getting in that cave

al_i_m_not_getting_in_that_cave.blurb: A small cluster of boulders at Rainbow Mountain in Madison, a suburb of Huntsville, tucked into the main group of blocks across from another named boulder. Seven problems, nearly all low-grade: most fall between V0 and V3, with a single one a notch harder. Rainbow Mountain as a whole is known for short approaches and easy problems, making it an after-work stop and a decent introduction to bouldering. Follow the trail toward the large balanced block to reach the main group and the cave boulder.

al_west_wall.blurb: The western established section of the Noccalula Falls gorge in Gadsden, on the north side of the creek, with sandstone walls. Seven routes: four are trad and three are sport, spanning roughly 5.8 to 5.11. Most lie in the 5.10 band, with a couple of harder 5.11 lines and one easier option. It is a sensible spot for a climber who wants a mix of gear and bolts at moderate grades. From the north lot, descend the wooden staircase and turn left at the bottom to reach the first line.

al_roadside_boulders_shelter_boulders.blurb: A small group of sandstone boulders at Horse Pens 40 near Steele, the first blocks you reach beside the road into the campground. The problems run from the easiest grades through a few real tests: a handful sit in the lower V grades, two near V7, and one hard problem around V9. Horse Pens 40 is known for sloping holds, good landings and a hardwood canopy, and friction is at its best in the cool part of the year. There is almost no walk, so it works as an easy start or a warm-down.

_expect.name: Rock that is Higher than I, The

al_rock_that_is_higher_than_i_the.blurb: The biggest cliff face near the parking area at Hurricane Creek Park in Tuscaloosa, standing behind a boulder known as the Joelder. Seven boulder problems on sandstone, all easy: four at V1, two at V2 and one at V3 at most. Cracks and underclings are the main hold types, so it suits beginners well. Follow the creek trail, bear right at the Joelder and head uphill behind it. The surrounding area has several faces and blocks of roughly 10 to 25 feet, which means some of the lines are tall for their grade.

al_deadwood_block.blurb: One of the boulders in the Sauta Cave bouldering area on the west side of Pine Mountain. It holds seven problems that range from V1 to V6, so there are a few warm-ups, a couple at V2, one at V3 and a pair of harder lines near the top end. The block is named after a big dead tree dragged in front of it. To find it, walk left past two other boulders. Getting to this part of the mountain is a bushwhack: the old trail has grown over, so allow extra time and route-finding up a gully.
